newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Jordan envoy resigns in Netanyahu spat.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Jordan envoy resigns in Netanyahu spat.

text.p: Israel's new ambassador to Jordan resigned on Tuesday after being kept in the dark by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu about a secret meeting the Israeli leader held with King Hussein.
Ambassador Oded Eran's resignation, confirmed by the Israeli Foreign Ministry, was the latest in a string of appointment blunders that have plagued Netanyahu's eleven-month tenure.

"I have no intention to be a censor or an obstacle to meetings but there is a need to brief the embassy on actions being taken," Israel radio quoted Eran as saying in a sharply worded letter of resignation.
Eran submitted his resignation only eight days after presenting his credentials to the Jordanian government in Amman.

An Israeli official who declined to be identified said Eran quit after Netanyahu kept his new appointee out of the loop about the meeting in the Jordanian Red Sea resort of Aqaba last Thursday over a water dispute.

"The Aqaba meeting was intended to be a secret meeting between the prime minister, King Hussein and Crown Prince Hassan in order to end the crisis between the countries on the water issue," Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak said in a statement.
"This is what was reported to the foreign minister, with an emphasis placed on the secrecy of the meeting...the matter was not intended to circumvent the Foreign Ministry or the embassy," Bazak said.
The statement promised that "from here on in, the matter will be dealt with, as has been customary, in full cooperation with the Foreign Ministry and the embassy".
Diplomatic sources said the summit was the latest in a chain of events, including plans for other high-level meetings, which Eran had not been consulted on.

"There is no room for my service here," the radio quoted Eran as saying in his letter. It said the ambassador complained that he could not expect good treatment in Jordan if his own government treated him poorly.

Foreign Minister David Levy said he would urge Eran to stay in his post: "I will do everything I can so that he will not resign because there is no reason for him to resign," Levy told Israel's Channel Two television.

The dispute over water rights granted to Jordan under a 1994 peace treaty caused the cancellation of a joint ceremony last week to commemorate seven Israeli girls shot dead by a Jordanian soldier in March.
Eran, formerly deputy director general for economic affairs at the Foreign Ministry, was Israel's second ambassador to Jordan after embassies were opened in the wake of a 1994 peace treaty.

In other Netanyahu appointment blunders, his appointee for justice minister stepped down last August after the attorney general ordered a probe into allegations he had in the past "influenced" a witness.

The Israeli leader's short-lived appointment of an attorney general in January sparked a corruption investigation in which police recommended Netanyahu be indicted for breach of public trust. The state prosecution elected not to indict Netanyahu due to insufficient evidence.
